test_title: PYST 2: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

This is the album who I found in the garage.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'who I found' i.e. this part has an error.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace **who **with **that**.
 
• The pronoun **who**, is an interrogative pronoun and a relative pronoun, used primarily to refer to **persons**.
 
 
• The musician **who **wrote this song is Canadian.
 
 
 
• **That **can be used for people, animals or things.
 
 
• Lisa wore the shoes **that **she bought in Italy.
 
 
 
• Hence, The correct answer is** option 3.**

 

**The correct sentence is**: This is the album ***that ***I found in the garage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**That vs. which**__

 
• **That **and **which **are used to start two different types of adjective clauses, called essential and non-essential clauses.
 
• **Essential clauses: That **always indicates a clause that is ***essential ***to the meaning of the sentence because it defines or identifies the noun it refers to. An essential clause does not take a comma before it.
 
 
• Lisa wore the shoes **that **she bought in Italy.
 
 
 
• **Non-essential clauses: Which **is used in a*** non-essential clause*** modifying *an animal or a thing*. A non-essential clause is one that gives secondary, non-essential information about a noun that is already fully identified. A non-essential clause is separated from its noun with a comma:
 
 
• Lisa wore her best leather shoes, **which **she bought in Italy.
